comments.comment: This video is amazing, its truly articulate, and I greatly appreciate that!  There are not enough women in this comment section, so here I am. I think that this subject is very touchy and that's why there aren't so many women here. Though my initial reaction was dismissal I decided to watch the video. I think there are certainly some valid points stated, especially because I see the education gap in my own experience. In a class of 30 there are two boys in my AP Literature class. In my AP Calculus class, there's likely more boys than girls, but maybe it's a 17:13 or so; it's not particularly drastic. While some part of me, the prideful part likely, wants to argue that there's still inequality in society for women—and there is—I also think that we do need to listen to men too. However, I think it's important to distinguish, we need to listen to men, when men are talking about men, or the human race as a whole. We need to listen to men when they're talking about wanting more support, but not when they talk of bringing women down, because I've seen the latter far too often recently. It can't be argued that NO men want women's inequality back, but it would also be unfair to say all men want that. I feel, and maybe this is just me, but I feel that we need to provide more support systems for men in areas where they are drastically unsupported. We need to do so without bringing down those supports for women. Finally, we need to change our attitudes because what causes inequality is fear of inequality the other way.  Sorry for the essay. Just my thoughts. If you disagree that's fine, but please do so respectfully; I am young and have a lot to learn, but berating is by no means teaching. Thank you for consideration.
